subject: physics
title: Power and efficiency
key_idea: Power is the rate of doing work, or the energy transferred each second. For a force moving an object at constant velocity, power = force × velocity. Efficiency is the useful output as a fraction of the total input.

blocks.text: Power says how quickly energy is transferred or work is done.

items.meaning: Work done per unit time. It is also the rate of energy transfer.
The unit of power. One watt is one joule per second.

blocks.label: Power
blocks.formula: P = W / t = E / t = ΔW / Δt

items: A machine with a power of 500 W transfers 500 J every second.
The same work done in less time means a greater power.
A kilowatt (kW) is 1000 W. A megawatt (MW) is 10⁶ W.
Power = work done ÷ time = energy transferred ÷ time.
The watt is one joule per second.

blocks.text: When a force moves an object at a steady speed, the power can be found from the force and the speed.

items.text: A constant force F moves an object a distance s in the direction of the force. Work done W = Fs.
Distance ÷ time is the velocity, v = s / t.

blocks.label: Power from force and velocity
where: F = force in the direction of motion, in N

diagram.alt: A practice calculation of the power needed to keep a car moving at a steady speed against a driving force.
diagram.question: A car travels at a steady {v} m/s. The driving force is {F} N. Calculate the power delivered, in kW.

items: At constant speed, the driving force equals the total resistive force.
The power needed to keep a vehicle moving therefore rises quickly with speed, because the resistive force also rises.
P = Fv for a force in the direction of motion.
At constant speed the driving force equals the resistive force.

blocks.text: No machine transfers all its input energy usefully. Efficiency measures how much it does.

blocks.label: Efficiency
blocks.formula: efficiency = useful energy output / total energy input = useful power output / total power input
where: Use the same units on top and bottom.
Multiply by 100 to give a percentage.

items: Efficiency is a ratio, so it has no unit.
It can be written as a fraction, a decimal or a percentage.
It is always less than 1 (100%), because some energy is always wasted, usually as thermal energy.
Energy is still conserved. Useful output + wasted output = total input.

items.text: A motor draws 800 W and lifts a load, gaining 600 W of useful power.
Efficiency = 75%. The wasted power is 200 W.

items: Efficiency = useful output ÷ total input, for energy or for power.
It has no unit and is always less than 100%.

checks.q: A crane lifts a 600 kg load through 15 m in 20 s. Calculate the useful power output of the crane.
A lorry travels at 22 m/s against a total resistive force of 5400 N. Calculate the power the engine delivers to the wheels.
checks.a: At constant speed the driving force equals the resistive force. P = Fv = 5400 × 22 = 119 000 W (about 120 kW).

checks.q: A motor takes 2500 J of electrical energy and does 1800 J of useful work. Calculate its efficiency and state where the rest of the energy goes.
checks.a: Efficiency = 1800 / 2500 = 0.72 (72%). The remaining 700 J is wasted, mostly as thermal energy to the surroundings.

items: Work done can be found for a **variable force**. It is the area under a force–displacement graph.
For a straight-line graph, use the area of a rectangle, triangle or trapezium. For a curve, count squares.
The energy transferred is W = Fs cos θ when the force is at an angle θ to the movement.
